chunks: For the animal, upon its owner, are six rights: he must not burden it beyond its strength; he must not use its back as a seat for conversations; he must begin by feeding it when he dismounts; he must not brand it; he must not strike it on its face, for indeed it glorifies (God); and he must offer water to it whenever he passes by it.

key_terms.الدابة: riding animal or beast of burden used for travel
key_terms.تسبيح: glorification of God, declaring His transcendence
key_terms.حقوق: rights — legally binding obligations owed to another

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a riding animal upon its owner in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) enumerates six specific obligations that an owner bears toward his riding animal. These rulings reflect the Shia jurisprudential tradition that animals deserve legal protections, and the theological rationale given — that the animal glorifies God — would have resonated deeply with an 8th-century audience who accepted the universal tasbih of creation. The hadith situates animal welfare within a framework of piety rather than mere utility.
